evidence.finding: Rigid-body rx/ry/rz, position, and velocity use 1/256 quantization; schema identity values of 1 are generic defaults and do not prove player dimensions.
Rigid-body bounds are stored as rx/ry/rz and used as half extents around px/py/pz. Constructor defaults are generic entity defaults, not confirmed player dimensions.
Player script position and rigid-body position are identical in both conversion directions. Combined with the symmetric rigid-body sweep, this confirms body-center coordinates.

Historical Player exports PLAYER_WIDTH=0.45 and PLAYER_HEIGHT=1.1. Camera and animation normalize body.ry by PLAYER_HEIGHT, and swept AABB expands center positions by rx/ry/rz, confirming upright default half extents 0.45x1.1x0.45.
Lokibox independently identifies rx/ry/rz as boundingBox and hsx/hsy/hsz as halfExtents on live Player state, proving that both field groups must be tracked separately.

The compatibility backend previously bound Player and RigidBody by identical ids while inheriting generic 1/1/1 bounds and shape identities. Project-package Player sessions now require and propagate the recovered upright default profile across both field groups.

Initial handshake, initial PUBLIC state, authoritative registration, runtime frames, and later PUBLIC states propagate independent bounds and shape half extents; PUBLIC production writes rx/ry/rz and hsx/hsy/hsz from separate profile fields.
The local body uses confirmed body-center coordinates, broadphase candidate bounds, and a separately tracked contact shape.
